newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-T&N to step out of shadow of asbestos.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-T&N to step out of shadow of asbestos.

text.p: British auto components group T&N Plc acted on Wednesday to relieve its shareholders of the burden of future asbestos litigation with an innovative insurance deal that will give it over 1.2 billion pounds ($2 billion) cover.
In a deal welcomed warmly by the London share market, T&N said it expected to remove the uncertainty linked to its past as an asbestos manufacturer and to unlock shareholder value.
"I really do think that at a stroke... we have produced the vision of an asbestos-free T&N," company chairman Sir Colin Hope told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The complex package centres around a huge 323 million pound transfer from its own reserves that will form the core of an "in-house" insurance fund providing 690 million pounds of cover.

On top of this total, determined by specialist actuaries as a fair assessment of the worst case outcome of all asbestos health claims it may face, T&N has bought a further cap from a consortium of three of the world's biggest reinsurance firms.
Their policy will provide the firm with a further 500 million pounds worth of cover for a one-off premium of 92 million -- and will be worldwide, without any time limit.

Looking to the prospect of finding 323 million pounds from cash over a three year period, Hope said it should be straighforward to generate this from operating cash flow and through continuing disposals of non-core businesses.

The arrangement should, therefore, remove the need for separate asbestos charges on the company's profit and loss accounts, in turn unshackling earnings per share and raising the affordability of its dividend payments (dividend cover).
Hope said this had important consequences for the way the company could address future dividend payments, saying, "It certainly does remove the constraints clearly."

"Obviously we're not making any promises as far as future dividends are concerned, but emphasising that cover will improve and it's a matter of ensuring that the operating performance continues to improve, and the cash flow is adequate to do it."

The engineering company's health liabilities date back to its past, when it was known as Turner & Newall, and mined and manufactured asbestos, used extensively in construction and automotive industries around the world earlier this century.
The actuarial analysis supporting the deal calculated the total of likely future losses, which the insurance industry dubs as risks "incurred but not yet reported" (IBNR).
Hope said it was likely that some funding and protection for claims would be probably be needed until 2020 or thereabouts.

However, in an added complication for the company, T&N has also decided to set aside an extra 50 million pounds in provisions for any old claims that might rebound if a disputed settlement system in the U.S. is cancelled.

T&N, which has advanced as an efficient and profitable manufacturer of automotive components since Hope took the chair in 1989, has already paid out about 300 million pounds for asbestos-related claims over a period of years.
Finance Director David Harding, interviewed on Reuters Financial Television, said he believed the share market could "now look to the value of the underlying business".

By 1215 GMT T&N's share price was up 32p at 176-1/2p, in turnover of nearly 10 million shares, as analysts agreed the moves allowed the market to remove the price discount built in to reflect the asbestos risks. ($1=.5990 Pound)
